partition_policy.training: all target facts except source-exclusive validation and blind facts

results.name: Side-effect profile indication transfer
results.hypothesis: A drug can inherit an indication from a treated peer when uncommon side effects form a substantial fraction of both drugs' bounded adverse-event profiles.
results.body: training-treated peer and candidate share at least 3 p90-specific side effects covering at least half of the smaller p90-bounded profile
results.mechanism_rationale: Side-effect similarity can fingerprint shared pharmacology, but it is indirect and may reflect reporting or class effects rather than the therapeutic mechanism.
results.trapi_notes: The treatment and side-effect paths are TRAPI-expressible; profile cardinality, overlap fraction, source exclusion, and ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (peer:Drug)-[treatment:TREATS|AMELIORATES_CONDITION]->(object:Disease)
WHERE any(
  source IN coalesce(treatment.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  WHERE NOT source IN ['infores:drug-repurposing-hub', 'infores:ttd']
)
  AND peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree >= 3
  AND peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <= 111
MATCH (peer)-[:HAS_SIDE_EFFECT]->(phenotype:PhenotypicFeature)
      <-[:HAS_SIDE_EFFECT]-(subject:Drug)
WHERE subject <> peer
  AND subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree >= 3
  AND subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <= 111
  AND phenotype._miner_side_effect_drug_degree <= 96
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
WITH subject, peer, object, count(DISTINCT phenotype) AS shared_count,
     CASE
       WHEN subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <
            peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
       THEN subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
       ELSE peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
     END AS smaller_profile
WHERE shared_count >= 3
  AND 2 * shared_count >= smaller_profile
RETURN DISTINCT subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id

results.name: Side-effect profile transfer without disease mimicry
results.hypothesis: Side-effect-profile indication transfer is more credible when the candidate drug does not reproduce an exact phenotype of the disease.
results.body: R135 excluding exact overlap between candidate side effects and disease phenotypes
results.mechanism_rationale: The gate removes an explicit adverse counter-mechanism but retains the indirect side-effect-similarity premise.
results.trapi_notes: The positive and negative graph motifs are TRAPI-expressible separately; profile overlap, exact absence, source exclusion, and ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (peer:Drug)-[treatment:TREATS|AMELIORATES_CONDITION]->(object:Disease)
WHERE any(
  source IN coalesce(treatment.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  WHERE NOT source IN ['infores:drug-repurposing-hub', 'infores:ttd']
)
  AND peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree >= 3
  AND peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <= 111
MATCH (peer)-[:HAS_SIDE_EFFECT]->(phenotype:PhenotypicFeature)
      <-[:HAS_SIDE_EFFECT]-(subject:Drug)
WHERE subject <> peer
  AND subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree >= 3
  AND subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <= 111
  AND phenotype._miner_side_effect_drug_degree <= 96
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
  AND NOT EXISTS {
    MATCH (subject)-[:HAS_SIDE_EFFECT]->(:PhenotypicFeature)
          <-[:HAS_PHENOTYPE]-(object)
  }
WITH subject, peer, object, count(DISTINCT phenotype) AS shared_count,
     CASE
       WHEN subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree <
            peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
       THEN subject._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
       ELSE peer._miner_side_effect_profile_degree
     END AS smaller_profile
WHERE shared_count >= 3
  AND 2 * shared_count >= smaller_profile
RETURN DISTINCT subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id

results.name: Chemical-class and side-effect profile transfer
results.hypothesis: Side-effect-profile transfer is more credible when candidate and treated peer also share a relatively specific chemical class.
results.body: R135 plus immediate chemical class containing at most 30 drugs
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule combines a pharmacological phenotype fingerprint with chemical ontology similarity, although neither establishes disease-corrective direction.
results.trapi_notes: The positive paths are TRAPI-expressible; profile overlap, shared-class identity, source exclusion, and degree constraints require post-processing.
